title: I built a neon bullet-heaven shooter entirely with Claude Code. Free to play in browser
author: ArthursoftDev
selftext:
**System Mainframe** is a bullet-heaven / roguelite where you play as a digital craft tasked with purging computer viruses and an AI mainframe gone rogue. Weapons fire automatically; you dodge, grab data, and pick upgrades on level-up. There's persistent upgrades, customisation and skills between levels to raise your power.

It's a bit of a mash up of games like Vampire Survivors and Geometry Wars with music/audio that dynamically changes based on your progress in a level. It gets really hectic and I think it does a great job tapping into that rapid level up dopamine rush, especially when using the shadow purge to destroy everything on screen!

**How it was made:** plain JavaScript, no engine. The code was written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) over a few days, with me directing design, playtesting, and tuning. Art is all code driven with geometric shapes. Claude doesn't always handle music very well but in this case I thought it did a really good job although I did have to bring in Fable a few times.

**Game content:**

* 5 sectors (worlds), 30+ nodes (levels), 9 boss fights
* 15 weapon types and modules with upgrades
* 6 ships (4 unlockable) with signature abilities
* Keyboard, Mouse, Gamepad and touch support
* 2-player local co-op (share a keyboard or two gamepads)
* 8 languages (machine translated)

It’s in Playgama’s sandbox right now, which is their testing stage before wider release, so honest feedback is genuinely useful. Especially: did the first minute hook you, and where did you stop playing?

Happy to answer questions about the AI workflow, what it was good at, where I had to step in etc.
